title: Apartheid and its end
examples: What were the main rules of apartheid?
How did people resist the apartheid laws?
What was important about the year 1994?

explain.say: Apartheid was a system of forced separation of people.
These laws separated people based on their race in South Africa.
Resistance included peaceful protests and acts of civil disobedience.
Nelson Mandela was a key leader in the fight against this system.
The year nineteen ninety-four marked the end of apartheid in South Africa.
In everyday life, we see this idea when people fight for equal rights today.

faq.a: Apartheid was a harsh system of racial segregation and discrimination enforced by the government. It meant that people were treated differently based on the color of their skin.
asks: Tell me about the rules of apartheid.

faq.q: Who was Nelson Mandela and why was he important?
faq.a: Nelson Mandela was a major anti-apartheid activist who spent many years imprisoned for his fight for equality. He became a global symbol of freedom and resistance.

faq.q: How did people resist apartheid peacefully?
faq.a: People resisted through organized protests, boycotts, and refusing to obey unfair laws. These actions showed the strength of the community's will.
asks: What were some forms of resistance?

faq.a: Nineteen ninety-four was the year of the first fully democratic, multi-racial election in South Africa. This election marked the official end of the apartheid system.

faq.q: Do these laws still exist anywhere?
faq.a: No, the laws of apartheid were officially dismantled and abolished by the government. The goal was to create a truly equal society.

facts: Apartheid was a system of institutionalized racial segregation.
The struggle against apartheid involved both non-violent and armed resistance.
Nelson Mandela was a key figure in the fight for democracy.
The first democratic election in South Africa occurred in 1994.

quiz.say: Apartheid laws primarily separated people based on what factor?
quiz.why: The system was fundamentally built upon racial classification and separation.

wrong.1: While wealth affected life, apartheid was based on birth-given race.
wrong.2: Religion was important, but the state laws targeted race specifically.
wrong.3: Job type was affected, but the core discrimination was racial.

quiz.say: What event marked the end of the apartheid system in South Africa?
quiz.why: This year saw the first multi-racial democratic election, ending the system.

wrong.1: This year saw major acts of resistance, but not the end.
wrong.2: This was a turning point, but the formal end came later.
wrong.3: The system was already dismantled before this date.

quiz.say: Which action best represents non-violent resistance against unjust laws?
quiz.why: Boycotts are a powerful, non-violent way to show disapproval of a system.

wrong.0: This is too vague; organized boycotts are a specific tactic.
wrong.1: This was not the primary, sustained form of resistance taught.
wrong.3: While some chose this, the movement heavily emphasized non-violence first.
